prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1231; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Can you confirm you're comfortable with us recording this call?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Please describe where you were and what you were doing when the collision happened.

A: I was driving home from work, heading south on the main road in Katy. It was late afternoon and traffic was moving slowly.

Q: Can you tell me what happened next?

A: The car in front of me stopped suddenly, so I braked. Then a vehicle coming the other way drifted into my lane and we collided head-on. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was enough to jolt me forward and back.

Q: How fast do you believe you were traveling at impact?

A: I'd say maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour. I had just slowed down when it happened.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?

A: No, I didn't hit my head. I stayed awake the whole time.

Q: Did you get medical attention after the collision?

A: Yes, a paramedic checked me at the scene, and then I went to an urgent care clinic later that evening because my neck was really sore.

Q: Where are you feeling pain or stiffness right now?

A: My neck and upper back are the worst. I also get headaches that start at the base of my skull, and my shoulders feel tight.

Q: Have you had any prior neck or back injuries?

A: No, nothing significant. I've had some general stiffness from sitting at a desk, but nothing that required treatment.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Just that I'm still going to physical therapy a few times a week, and I'm keeping track of my symptoms in case you need more details.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.

A: Thank you.
